text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian dailies. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Hague war crimes tribunal begins trial of Bosnian Croat general Tihomir Blaskic exactly 15 months after he voluntarily surrendered to the court.
- G7 countries and Russia want better implementation of the peace accord for Bosnia and express their dissatisfaction with a sluggish process of returning refugees and displaced people.
- The Paneuropean Transport Conference in Helsinki expected to approve connecting Croatia's main road corridors to the Trans-European Networks (TEN).
- Croatia will have a wheat crop of 825,000 tonnes this year. National demand estimated at an annual 550,000 tonnes.
- Some 130,000 eligible beneficiaries of mass voucher privatisation scheme registered in the first three weeks.
- Health Ministry will pass a new list of 680 medicines patients in Croatia can obtain free of charge from July 1.
- Why do you allow obscure newspapers to use you as a factor of destabilisation, President Tudjman writes to academician Ivan Supek in an open letter.
- Teachers' training may be shortened to three from four years to resolve a critical shortage.
- Ante Nobilo, lawyer of the Bosnian Croat Tihomir Blaskic, says the defence had found false witnesses against Blaskic.

- Constitutional court flooded by complaints against the law on reprivatisation of property that was nationalised during the Yugoslav communist regime. Authorities warn the deadline for presenting claims for nationalised property is June 30.
- With good organisation we can detect and stop misuse of information systems, says Ognjen Haramina, organiser of a course on computer crime held in Dubrovnik in cooperation with the Scotland Yard.
- G7 summit in Colorado: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel praised Bosnian Croats for making most progress in the implementation of the Dayton peace agreements. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
